inventions: The outcrop: a fin of darker, harder stone standing out of the mountain at the bench's inner edge forty paces behind the ledge's root, a man high and three carts long, with a down-slope lee; Seln has it as ground before anyone speaks; the herd's split point measured afterward at eleven paces up-slope of its face; the lattice's scorch left as 'thirty paces of scorched shale' across the face above it.

The collapse's extent: three carts' length of the ledge, a cart's width, gone into the gorge; what remains is a lip against the bulge that a walker can take with hands on the rock and a mule or cart cannot — the map's last finding (the traverse does not hold a cart), and the way Oryn reaches them on foot with the mule left beyond the bulge where the bench opens.

The herd's flight staged as Chapter 5's derivation refined by the event: a step went uphill, a run cannot (the shelf cannot hold thirty at a run; the outer plates go), so the herd comes off the upper bench down the face in a front two hundred paces wide, in two waves along the slant of its line — sixteen past the fin first, fourteen later at the cart; three heard going into the gorge and not sworn to; twenty-seven down the mountain toward the fan, and by the carter's report onto the low road.

Cael's held wants under the herd, with the reason priced in one beat: Compression at contact to take the shoulder; Anchor to fix the cart to the mountain; refused because a second declaration under the second half would turn it toward the fin. No Shadow.

Lira's leg broken by terrain, not by an animal: a plate going out under her foot as the shelf shifted under the second wave, the leg into the gap, the plate above coming down on it; her boot lost with the ledge; the tape from that morning still on the bare ankle. Splinted on the first day with two plates of the mountain and Karis's cord.
Brom pulling both boxes with the bound arm (the hand allowed to hold, not pull), the wrist reopening under the cloth; he rewraps it one-handed with his teeth and checks the boxes before his arm.

The two days of waiting: fire lit with a flint because the Ember practitioner is asleep against a box; the road food gone with the cart and Brom stretching a day and a half of pack food to three; Cael sleeping on the middle box on his right side, counting the breaths that stop, not taking the log out because he could not hold it; Seln walking the remnant lip in the afternoon, doing the healer arithmetic (Oxhollow two days on for a walker; no healer of its own; the route-walking healer four days from anywhere), and packing to go at first light of the second day, refusing to walk new shale in the dark.

Oryn's kit, mule, and manner: a mule with panniers left beyond the bulge; a carter's coat; a leather roll of tools; a water-skin she empties by half in a morning; the walk that does not change pace at the narrow place or the wide; her hands as the first thing catalogued; her lines in the clinical register ('I'll be the one who says that', 'Then it went as far as it went. That's not straight.', 'That's one', 'It's not a dog's business now. It's yours.', 'Hm.' as a verdict on the lattice scorch); Seln asking 'Tier' and her answer 'Iron. Four, if anybody's keeping a book up here.'

The carter's report as she gives it: into Oxhollow off the void road at noon on the day of the collapse; the shale-backs down on the low road at a run; the traverse crew overdue off it; she was at the ford.

The mending as observed from outside: Lira's 'Cold' and 'It's going along'; the swelling going down 'as water goes out of a basin when the plug is pulled'; the two lines of the shin becoming one; the whole from kneeling to hands-off under an hour; Oryn's face the colour of the shale, wet at the temples, sitting 'as a carter sets down a load he knows the weight of to the pound'.

Oryn's surface readings on Brom and Karis naming the Path beneath the hurt ('Iron Skin'; 'Ember') — per the architecture's definition of the surface reading (finds injury and the Path beneath it) — so that 'nothing' on Cael is a contrast the reader can hear. She asks nothing about the lattice or the scars.

Cael's comparison set for the instrument-face: his own Kindling ('At fourteen, for eleven seconds, from the inside'), assessors at Ardenmere and Greyvane, the Halcenvane panel; 'Healers did not read the page. Healers read the leg.' And 'four healers in four years' as his count of healers he has been under.
Lira's line for the cause, and Karis's ordering of it ('The ledge went. Then it was you.' / 'Then it was me.'), held without further comment.
